confidence_note: Book text not read; chapter titles and ideas come from summaries (readingraphics, lifeclub). Summary examples (jealousy at a party, final week) may not be Singer's own. The old text's federal-investigation story belongs to The Surrender Experiment (2015), not this book, and is omitted; no personal Singer anecdote is used. Spiritual teaching, no measurement.
facts: Part III, Freeing Yourself, has chapters 'Let Go Now or Fall', 'Removing Your Inner Thorn', 'Stealing Freedom for Your Soul' and 'Pain, the Price of Freedom'; Part IV includes 'Letting Go of False Solidity'; Part V includes 'The Spiritual Path of Nonresistance'.
A summary quotes: 'The prerequisite to true freedom is to decide that you do not want to suffer anymore.'
Part III teaches releasing fears and disturbances as early as possible; negative thoughts are to pass through you and float on by.

The personal self functions like a cage consciousness cannot get out of; animals in small zoo cages illustrate being trapped in your own self; clinging to thoughts builds the cage; being absorbed in a film so you forget your surroundings is compared to clinging.
A summary example: seeing your partner talk to someone else at a party upsets you; reflecting on your own death shows that their happiness matters more than the argument.
In 'Contemplating Death', a summary says: imagine you will die in a week, then ask why you are not doing those things now.
It is a spiritual teaching; no measurement is mentioned.
scene_details: a thought that passes through and floats on by

tension: The book says freedom starts with a decision not to suffer, yet clinging builds the cage.
opening_idea: A line quoted from the book: the prerequisite to true freedom is to decide that you do not want to suffer anymore.

lessons.idea: Decide you are done suffering over one thing and let the thought pass instead of holding it.
lessons.anchor: the cage built by clinging to thoughts

reflect_final: Which one thing would you decide, this week, to stop suffering over, even before you know how?

use_cases.situation: A sour exchange replays in your head all evening
use_cases.move: Say it can pass through and decline to replay it again tonight.

use_cases.situation: A friend has stewed over a slight for days
use_cases.move: Ask whether carrying it still does anything for them.

use_cases.situation: Your partner laughs with someone else at a party and you feel the sting
use_cases.move: Name the sting, let it pass and talk about something real later.
